slides.title: 5 Thanksgiving leftover myths to drop before you eat them

slides.myth: Let leftovers cool on the counter before the fridge.
slides.fact: Hot food can go straight into the fridge. Split big batches into shallow containers and get them in within 2 hours.
slides.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

slides.myth: Leftover turkey is good for a week.
slides.fact: Eat cooked leftovers within 3 to 4 days, or freeze them. After that, toss them.
slides.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

slides.myth: If it smells fine, it's safe to eat.
slides.fact: The bacteria that make people sick usually can't be seen, smelled or tasted. Go by the days, not your nose.
It only puts them to sleep. Freezing keeps food safe, but once it thaws, the bacteria can become active again.
slides.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

slides.myth: Hot to the touch means it's reheated enough.
slides.fact: Reheat leftovers to 165°F on a food thermometer. Bring gravy and soups to a rolling boil.
slides.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
